q:
(*) Physical exam in initial pyloric stenosis expect:
A. Bouvert sign
B. Less sign
C. Gastric clapotment
D. Blumberg sign
E. Kussmaul sign
a:
d ?? none of these signs are mentioned anywhere
(stenic phase = first -> stomach fighting stenosis, few symptoms)
(atonic phase = stomach evacuation failure syndrome -> main symptoms occur)

✅ Correct: A
—————————————————————————
✅ A. Correct. Bouveret sign (palpable olive in the epigastrium) is a classic finding in pyloric stenosis, therefore this is the single correct answer in this SCQ context.
❌ B. Incorrect. Less sign is not associated with pyloric stenosis.
❌ C. Incorrect. Gastric clapotment (succussion splash) may appear, but it is not the primary expected exam finding chosen when only one answer is allowed.
❌ D. Incorrect. Blumberg sign indicates peritoneal irritation, not pyloric stenosis.
❌ E. Incorrect. Kussmaul sign relates to jugular venous pressure changes, not pyloric stenosis.
—————————————————————————

For pyloric stenosis, the only meaningful physical exam maneuvers are:


1. Palpation for the “olive”
Firm, mobile, olive-shaped mass in the right upper abdomen/epigastrium.
2. Observation of visible gastric peristalsis
Left-to-right peristaltic waves across the upper abdomen after feeding.
That’s it. Everything else is noise. Diagnosis is ultimately confirmed by ultrasound.
